title: 2D Battlefield in browser real world locations
author: Mallock78
selftext:
Hello,

I've posted previously about Global Operations: Drop Zone. With the help of Astra I've been able to make great progress for the visuals using Blender MCP.

I’m at the point now where the game actually works and I’ve mostly been playing it against bots. It’s already fun, but bots still do fairly sensible things. They push objectives, shoot, drive vehicles and generally fight the way they’re supposed to. What I really want to see now is what happens when the battlefield is full of actual people instead. Is it fun?

Even one proper 8v8 match would be really interesting to see. 32v32 would be the real test though: complete chaos on a battlefield based on real OpenStreetMap data.

It has player classes; Assault, Medic, Engineer. A store where you can buy upgrades with in game currency. Operator customization etc. 

At the moment server is running cheaply with 2 vCPUs so I’ve also added a queue system in case more people try to join than it can comfortably handle. Part of this test is honestly seeing where it starts falling over. 

I would love to have feedback of how it plays and please not the server is in Europe so feedback from lag compensation how it works if you are joining from another continent is there visible rubber banding etc.

DM me for the game link or google it. See you in the Drop Zone!

comments.author: Party_Sand_1337
comments.body: It looks cool! I'm curious was service are you using for multiplayer?

replies.author: Mallock78
replies.body: Thanks it's a custom made C# backend that generates the game map from OpenStreetMap data and renders the graphics that is then handed to the client that is made with Phaser. Gameplay is fully server authorative.

comments.author: Pizzaman2948
comments.body: How do building and trees generate from openstreet? Are they approximated because i thought only popular locations have that level of detail?

replies.author: Mallock78
replies.body: Backend uses biome data from OSM and then populate it procedurally. It's quite rudimentary at the moment but expanding the biome variations with desert etc. is in the backlog.

comments.author: truongan2101
comments.body: Did you download the OSM data first, then convert to the map for ofline running, or this is real time OSM loading?

replies.author: Mallock78
replies.body:
It's live OSM, not a pre-baked offline extract. When a match gets deployed at some coordinates, the server fires off an Overpass query for that bounding box and pulls buildings, roads, water and POIs right then, converts it into the tile map, and spawns the round. 

So no bundled map data, no offline conversion step. It only happens once per location though: the parsed layout gets cached in memory and in the database keyed by coords/zoom/scale, so if anyone plays that spot again it loads instantly from cache and only brand new locations actually hit OSM.
